day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Vancouver Airport at 12:00 PM — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Canada Line SkyTrain from YVR to downtown Vancouver (approx. $4.55 CAD), a budget-friendly and scenic 25-minute ride. Check in to Vancouver Harbour Stay and get settled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Granville Island Public Market Food Tour (self-guided to save money). Stroll through the vibrant market, sample artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, local baked goods, and seasonal produce from vendor stalls. Pick up affordable snacks and take in the buskers and waterfront atmosphere. Take the $3.75 mini-ferry from downtown to Granville Island for a fun, cheap water crossing.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take transit to Davie Street or Robson Street to explore the neighbourhood near the harbour. Enjoy a relaxed evening stroll along the downtown waterfront near Canada Place, taking in views of the North Shore mountains at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and pastry at the airport before landing (~$5–8 CAD)
meals.lunch: Granville Island Public Market — build your own affordable lunch from vendor stalls: fresh bread, deli meats, fruit, and a sampler bite or two (~$12–15 CAD)
meals.dinner: Japadog on Robson Street — iconic Vancouver street food, Japanese-style hot dogs from ~$7–10 CAD. Quick, delicious, and a true local experience.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the noon arrival. Focus on settling in, orienting yourself, and enjoying a casual food market afternoon. Buy a Compass Card at the SkyTrain station for easy, discounted transit all trip (~$6 card + load $20–30).

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Walk — rent a bike from Spokes Bicycle Rentals near the park entrance (~$10–15/hour or ~$30–40 for a half-day). Ride the iconic 10km seawall loop around Stanley Park, stopping to explore old-growth forest trails, Beaver Lake, totem poles at Brockton Point, and stunning ocean views toward the Lions Gate Bridge. Arrive early (by 9 AM) to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return the bike and explore Stanley Park on foot — visit the free rose garden and walk the forest trails. Afterward, head to Denman Street just outside the park for a leisurely browse of local cafes and shops. Rest your legs at a waterfront bench along English Bay Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Davie Street in the West End neighbourhood — a lively, welcoming local strip with affordable restaurants. Browse the area and enjoy the casual neighbourhood vibe before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bagel and coffee from a local café near Vancouver Harbour Stay (~$6–9 CAD) or pick up groceries from a nearby Safeway or Save-On-Foods for a DIY breakfast to save money.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Stanley Park — stop at a Denman Street deli or grab supplies from a nearby grocery store. Fresh sandwiches, fruit, and a drink for ~$10–12 CAD.
meals.dinner: Stepho's Souvlaki Greek Taverna on Davie Street — a Vancouver institution famous for massive, affordable Greek portions. Expect to spend ~$15–20 CAD. Arrive before 6 PM to avoid the lineup.

day_by_day.notes: June weather in Vancouver is typically mild (15–20°C) with occasional light rain — bring a light rain jacket just in case. The seawall is best enjoyed in the morning before tourist crowds and tour groups arrive. Bike rental shops open around 8–9 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre Hike — take transit from downtown (Bus 228 or 229 from Lonsdale Quay, reached via SeaBus from Waterfront Station, total transit ~$5–6 CAD round trip). The suspension bridge and Ecology Centre are FREE — a fantastic budget alternative to the pricey Capilano Bridge. Cross the bridge over the dramatic canyon, explore old-growth temperate rainforest trails, and visit the free Ecology Centre to learn about the local ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking the Lynn Canyon trail network — the 30-Foot Pool trail and Twin Falls trail are both free, beautiful, and well-marked (1–2 hours total). Return to North Vancouver via SeaBus and explore the Lonsdale Quay Market on the North Shore waterfront for a budget-friendly browse and snack.
day_by_day.evening: Return to downtown Vancouver via SeaBus (scenic 12-minute crossing with great skyline views — included in your Compass Card fare). Explore Gastown, Vancouver's oldest neighbourhood — cobblestone streets, the famous steam clock, and local boutiques. Great for an evening wander.

meals.breakfast: DIY breakfast at accommodation or a Tim Hortons near the hotel (~$5–7 CAD for coffee and a breakfast sandwich).
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from a grocery store the night before — sandwiches, trail mix, and water for the hike (~$8–10 CAD). There are picnic tables near the Lynn Canyon park entrance.
meals.dinner: Gastown area — try The Noodle Box on Robson Street or a pho restaurant in nearby Chinatown (a 5-minute walk from Gastown). A large bowl of pho or noodles runs ~$13–16 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy walking shoes or hiking boots for Lynn Canyon — some trail sections can be muddy in June. The SeaBus runs frequently (every 15–30 min) and the crossing itself is a highlight. Lynn Canyon Park is open daily and always free — no booking required.

day_by_day.morning: Cypress Mountain Hiking Trail — take a budget-friendly transit and taxi/rideshare combo up to Cypress Mountain (bus to Park Royal in West Vancouver, then a short rideshare up the mountain, ~$15–20 total). In June, enjoy self-guided alpine hiking on the Howe Sound Crest Trail or the easier Yew Lake Loop (free, no lift ticket needed in summer). Stunning panoramic views of Howe Sound, the city, and the Gulf Islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Vancouver and revisit Granville Island for any last-minute food souvenirs — local jams, smoked salmon, or artisan snacks make great affordable keepsakes. Walk the seawall from Granville Island back toward Yaletown for a scenic final afternoon in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vancouver — head to Commercial Drive ('The Drive') by transit for a vibrant, local, non-touristy neighbourhood experience. Browse indie shops and enjoy a farewell dinner at one of the many affordable international restaurants the street is famous for.

meals.breakfast: Café Medina on Beatty Street (a Vancouver favourite) — slightly splurge-worthy for the last day, Belgian waffles and coffee ~$18–22 CAD. Arrive when it opens to avoid a long wait.
meals.lunch: Granville Island — grab a fresh crepe, fish taco, or a bowl of chowder from market vendors (~$10–14 CAD).
meals.dinner: Commercial Drive — Havana Restaurant for Cuban-inspired food and a lively atmosphere (~$18–22 CAD), or try one of the many Italian or Ethiopian spots along the strip for ~$14–18 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm Cypress Mountain summer trail access and hours before going — trails are free but road conditions and shuttle availability can vary in early June. If weather is poor on Day 4, swap Cypress Mountain for a morning at the Vancouver Art Gallery (check for free admission days or pay-what-you-can evenings) or explore Chinatown and Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden (free outer garden).

trip_options.title: Classic Vancouver Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

A true West Coast wilderness experience just 30 minutes from downtown.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Allow time for baggage claim, ground transportation, and check-in at Vancouver Harbour Stay. The hotel's harbour-adjacent location makes it easy to get oriented quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll along the Vancouver Harbour waterfront. Walk through Gastown, Vancouver's oldest neighbourhood, exploring the cobblestone streets, the famous Steam Clock, and local boutique shops. This low-key orientation walk helps you get a feel for the city without overcommitting on arrival day.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Granville Island Public Market area or nearby False Creek for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the vibrant Yaletown neighbourhood, a short walk or transit ride from the harbour, known for its converted warehouse restaurants and patios.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a light snack at Vancouver International Airport (YVR) before departure gate.
meals.lunch: After check-in, try Cactus Club Cafe on Robson Street — a beloved Vancouver mid-range chain with fresh Pacific Northwest ingredients, burgers, and seafood bowls. Budget approx. CAD $20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Dine at The Flying Pig in Yaletown — a popular local bistro known for creative comfort food, charcuterie boards, and BC wines. Expect CAD $35–50 per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day is intentionally light. Prioritize hydration and rest after the flight. If arriving from a distant time zone, avoid heavy activities. Pick up a Compass Card (transit card) at the airport SkyTrain station to use throughout your trip — it will save money on buses and SkyTrain rides.

day_by_day.morning: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour — Head to Granville Island via the False Creek Aquabus ferry (a fun 5-minute ride from downtown). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the vibrant public market, sampling local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, handmade chocolates, baked goods, and seasonal BC produce. Chat with vendors and soak in the lively atmosphere unique to Vancouver's food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Walk — Rent a bike from one of the rental shops near the Denman Street entrance to Stanley Park (approx. CAD $15–25/hour). Ride the iconic 10km seawall loop around the park, stopping to explore old-growth forest trails, Beaver Lake, the totem poles at Brockton Point, and sweeping views of the North Shore mountains and harbour. Allow 2.5–3 hours at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Kissa Tanto or Bao Bei for Local Asian-Fusion Cuisine — Make a reservation in advance at either Kissa Tanto (Japanese-Italian fusion in a gorgeous vintage setting) or Bao Bei (inventive Chinese brasserie) in Chinatown. Both represent Vancouver's celebrated multicultural food scene and offer a memorable dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Thierry Café or a nearby bakery near the hotel before heading out — try a croissant and coffee. Budget CAD $10–15.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Granville Island Public Market itself — assemble a delicious spread of market samples and small bites from vendors (smoked salmon, fresh bread, cheese, fruit). Budget CAD $20–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Kissa Tanto or Bao Bei in Chinatown — Budget CAD $45–65 per person including cocktails. Reserve ahead as both are highly popular.

day_by_day.notes: The Aquabus ferry to Granville Island departs from multiple downtown stops including the Hornby Street dock — check the schedule online. Stanley Park bike rentals are plentiful near the park entrance on Denman Street. June weather in Vancouver is typically mild (15–20°C) with possible light rain — pack a light jacket and layers.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre Hike — Take a short drive or bus ride (approx. 30–40 minutes via transit) to Lynn Canyon Park in North Vancouver. Unlike the commercialized Capilano Bridge, Lynn Canyon's suspension bridge is completely free. Hike through stunning old-growth temperate rainforest, cross the suspension bridge over the dramatic canyon gorge, and visit the Ecology Centre to learn about the local ecosystem. Allow 3–4 hours for a thorough exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cypress Mountain Hiking Trail — Drive up to Cypress Mountain Provincial Park (approx. 20–30 minutes from Lynn Canyon or 30 minutes from downtown Vancouver) for a self-guided alpine hiking experience. In June, trails like the Howe Sound Crest Trail or the shorter Eagle Bluffs Trail offer breathtaking panoramic views of Howe Sound, the Gulf Islands, and Greater Vancouver. Allow 2–3 hours depending on your chosen trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Vancouver and spend a relaxed evening in the Kitsilano neighbourhood. Browse the boutique shops along 4th Avenue, enjoy the sunset views over English Bay from Kitsilano Beach, and dine locally.

meals.breakfast: Café Medina near downtown Vancouver — famous for their Belgian waffles, shakshuka, and lavender latte. A Vancouver institution. Budget CAD $20–30. Arrive early or expect a short wait.
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch from a nearby grocery store (Whole Foods or a local deli) before heading to Lynn Canyon — think sandwiches, fruit, trail mix, and water. Budget CAD $15–20. Alternatively, grab a bite at the Lynn Canyon Café near the park entrance.
meals.dinner: Nook Restaurant in Kitsilano — a cozy neighbourhood Italian spot known for wood-fired pizza and fresh pasta at reasonable prices. Budget CAD $30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cypress Mountain is accessible by car (rental recommended for this day) or by the seasonal Cypress Mountain shuttle bus from Park Royal Shopping Centre in West Vancouver — check current schedule. Wear sturdy walking shoes for both hikes. Bring sunscreen, water, and a windproof layer as alpine temperatures can be cooler even in June. Lynn Canyon is free to enter — a great budget-friendly nature highlight.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a slow, unhurried morning. Take a walk along the Vancouver Harbour seawall from your hotel toward Canada Place for sweeping views of the North Shore mountains and cruise ship activity. Visit the nearby Vancouver Convention Centre rooftop garden and stop at the Bill Reid Gallery of Northwest Coast Art if interested in Indigenous culture (approx. 1 hour, CAD $13 admission).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Granville Island or Chinatown area for final souvenir shopping and a last taste of Vancouver's food scene. Visit the Vancouver Chinatown Night Market (if operating on this date in June) or browse the shops on Main Street's 'antique row' for unique local finds. If time allows, relax at Queen Elizabeth Park for panoramic city views and beautifully manicured gardens — free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner in Vancouver. Choose a spot that encapsulates the city's Pacific Northwest identity with fresh, locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at Jam Café (if you haven't tried it) or return to a favourite spot from earlier in the trip. Alternatively, try Purebread Bakery near Gastown for exceptional pastries and coffee. Budget CAD $12–18.
meals.lunch: Grab a casual lunch at Tacofino on Robson Street or nearby — a beloved Vancouver taco and burrito spot with fresh Pacific flavours. Budget CAD $15–22.
meals.dinner: Miku Restaurant on the waterfront near Canada Place — known for its award-winning Aburi (flame-seared) sushi and stunning harbour views. A slightly elevated but worthwhile mid-range splurge for your last night. Budget CAD $55–80 per person. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure logistics today — confirm flight times, airport transfer options (Canada Line SkyTrain from Waterfront Station is the most convenient and affordable option to YVR, approx. 25 minutes, CAD $4–9 depending on zone). Leave at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Vancouver's Canada Line runs frequently and is the recommended airport transfer from the harbour area.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vancouver Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Granville Island Public Market, sampling local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, handmade pastries, and BC wines. Chat with local vendors and discover the best of Vancouver's food scene in one iconic waterfront location.

experiences.description: Experience Vancouver's celebrated Asian-fusion dining scene in Chinatown. Enjoy inventive dishes blending Japanese-Italian or modern Chinese flavors using locally sourced BC ingredients. This neighborhood is the cultural and culinary heart of the city.

experiences.name: Cypress Mountain Snowshoe or Hiking Trail
experiences.description: Take a short drive up to Cypress Mountain for a guided or self-guided snowshoe trek (winter) or alpine hiking trail (summer) with panoramic views of Vancouver, the Strait of Georgia, and the Gulf Islands. A true West Coast wilderness experience just 30 minutes from downtown.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight AC lands at 12:00 PM. Transfer via private luxury car service to Vancouver Harbour Stay. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll along the waterfront promenade adjacent to the hotel to soak in the harbour views and begin settling into the city's atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour: Head to Granville Island (approx. 15-min taxi or water taxi from the harbour) for an immersive guided food tour of the iconic Public Market. Sample artisan cheeses, freshly smoked Pacific salmon, local charcuterie, hand-crafted chocolates, and seasonal BC produce. Engage with local vendors and learn about Vancouver's vibrant food culture in a relaxed, premium small-group setting.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Kissa Tanto or Bao Bei for Local Asian-Fusion Cuisine: Experience Vancouver's celebrated Chinatown dining scene with a reservation at Kissa Tanto (upscale Italian-Japanese fusion in a stunning 1960s supper-club setting) or Bao Bei (inventive modern Chinese brasserie). Enjoy expertly crafted cocktails, seasonal tasting menus, and the warm ambiance of one of Canada's most acclaimed dining destinations.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light meal on the plane or grab a premium coffee and pastry at the hotel upon arrival — no formal breakfast scheduled given the midday arrival.
meals.lunch: Granville Island Public Market: Graze on artisan food stalls — smoked salmon on sourdough, aged BC cheeses, fresh-pressed juices, and handmade empanadas as part of the food tour experience.
meals.dinner: Kissa Tanto or Bao Bei, Chinatown — budget CAD $120–$160 per person including cocktails and a curated tasting menu.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a private luxury airport transfer and confirm restaurant reservations at Kissa Tanto well in advance — it is one of Vancouver's hardest tables to secure. The water taxi from the harbour to Granville Island is a scenic and enjoyable option (approx. 20 min). Pack light layers as June evenings in Vancouver can be mild but breezy near the water.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Walk: Begin the morning with a premium bike rental (or private guided cycling experience) along the iconic 10km Stanley Park Seawall. Depart from the Coal Harbour entrance, just minutes from the hotel. Stop to explore old-growth forest trails, visit Siwash Rock, enjoy panoramic views of the North Shore mountains, and pause at Prospect Point for sweeping vistas of the Lions Gate Bridge and Burrard Inlet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stanley Park Forest Immersion & Totem Poles: After completing the seawall, venture into the interior of Stanley Park on foot. Visit the historic totem poles at Brockton Point, walk the quieter forest trails beneath towering Douglas firs and western red cedars, and enjoy the tranquility of Lost Lagoon. Stop at the Vancouver Aquarium (optional premium add-on) for a curated behind-the-scenes marine experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Cocktails & Fine Dining at a Waterfront Restaurant: Return to the harbour area and enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at the hotel bar or a rooftop lounge overlooking the water. Dine at Ancora Waterfront Dining & Patio (Coal Harbour location) — a Peruvian-Japanese fusion restaurant with stunning harbour views, exceptional ceviche, premium wagyu, and an award-winning wine list perfectly suited to a luxury evening.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel premium breakfast at Vancouver Harbour Stay — enjoy eggs Benedict with smoked BC salmon, fresh fruit, and single-origin pour-over coffee overlooking the harbour.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a curated gourmet takeaway near Stanley Park (e.g., Forage Restaurant grab-and-go or Raincity Grill) — artisan sandwiches, charcuterie, and local sparkling water enjoyed on the seawall.
meals.dinner: Ancora Waterfront Dining & Patio, Coal Harbour — budget CAD $150–$200 per person including wine pairings and a full tasting menu.

day_by_day.notes: Stanley Park is a short 10-minute cycle or walk from the hotel, making this a very convenient full-day experience. June offers long daylight hours (sunset around 9:15 PM), so the evening harbour views will be spectacular. Reserve Ancora well in advance and request a patio table for the best waterfront experience.

day_by_day.morning: Cypress Mountain Alpine Hiking Trail: Arrange a private luxury transfer (approx. 30–40 min from downtown) up to Cypress Mountain on the North Shore. In June, the alpine meadows are in full bloom with wildflowers and the trails offer breathtaking panoramic views of Howe Sound, the Gulf Islands, and Vancouver Island. Choose from guided alpine hikes on the Howe Sound Crest Trail or the scenic Black Mountain Loop — ideal for nature lovers seeking an immersive wilderness experience without extreme difficulty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre Hike: After descending from Cypress, continue to nearby Lynn Canyon (approx. 20-min drive) for a guided hike through old-growth temperate rainforest. Cross the free suspension bridge dramatically strung over Lynn Canyon's rushing creek, explore the Ecology Centre to learn about the coastal rainforest ecosystem, and walk the quieter canyon trails away from the crowds. This pairing of two North Shore natural gems makes for an exceptional half-day in the wilderness.
day_by_day.evening: Refined Tasting Menu Dinner in Yaletown: Return to the city and change for a premium evening. Dine at Blue Water Cafe in Yaletown — Vancouver's premier seafood institution. Enjoy a celebrated raw bar featuring Dungeness crab, BC spot prawns, and Pacific oysters, followed by a chef's tasting menu spotlighting the finest local seafood. Pair with selections from their extensive 1,000-label wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoked salmon eggs royale, fresh-pressed green juice, and house-baked pastries before the morning mountain departure.
meals.lunch: Pre-packed premium trail lunch prepared by the hotel or a local caterer — think charcuterie boards, artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, BC apple slices, and dark chocolate, enjoyed with a mountain view at a scenic rest point on Cypress Mountain.
meals.dinner: Blue Water Cafe, Yaletown — budget CAD $180–$230 per person including the chef's tasting menu and wine pairings. Reserve the chef's table for an immersive kitchen-front experience.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private vehicle transfer for the full North Shore day — a driver who can wait or shuttle between Cypress and Lynn Canyon is highly recommended for a seamless luxury experience. Wear sturdy hiking footwear and bring layers; alpine temperatures at Cypress can be 5–8°C cooler than downtown even in June. BC spot prawn season typically peaks in May–June, making Blue Water Cafe's raw bar an exceptional seasonal treat.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Harbour Morning & Floatplane Scenic Flight: Begin the final morning with a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Then, walk minutes from the hotel to Vancouver Harbour Flight Centre for a premium scenic floatplane flight over the city, Stanley Park, the Gulf Islands, and the snow-capped Coast Mountains. This 20–30 minute aerial experience offers an unparalleled perspective on Vancouver's extraordinary natural setting and is a fitting luxury finale to the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Curated Shopping & Neighbourhood Exploration in Gastown & Yaletown: Spend the afternoon exploring Vancouver's most characterful neighbourhoods. Browse premium boutiques, Indigenous art galleries, and design stores in Gastown (cobblestone streets, the iconic steam clock, and heritage brick buildings). Continue to Yaletown for upscale lifestyle boutiques and a coffee at one of the neighbourhood's specialty cafés. Pick up artisan gifts — smoked salmon, local honey, BC wine, or Indigenous artwork — as premium souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner at Hawksworth Restaurant: Conclude the trip in style with a farewell dinner at Hawksworth Restaurant in the Rosewood Hotel Georgia — consistently ranked among Canada's finest restaurants. Chef David Hawksworth's contemporary Canadian cuisine celebrates the finest local and seasonal ingredients with technical brilliance. Enjoy a full tasting menu with optional wine or cocktail pairings in an elegant, timeless dining room.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel breakfast — full à la carte spread including smoked salmon Benedict, truffle scrambled eggs, fresh-pressed juices, and a cheese and charcuterie board. Take your time before the floatplane departure.
meals.lunch: Light and relaxed lunch in Gastown — try The Keefer Bar for creative cocktails and small plates, or Pidgin Restaurant for refined Pacific Rim small plates in a stylish setting. Budget CAD $60–$80 per person.
meals.dinner: Hawksworth Restaurant, Downtown Vancouver — budget CAD $200–$260 per person for the full tasting menu with wine pairings. Request a corner booth for the most intimate farewell dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm floatplane booking with Harbour Air or Seair Seaplanes well in advance — scenic flights sell out quickly in summer. Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if the flight departs later in the evening. Hawksworth accepts reservations 60 days in advance; book immediately upon trip confirmation. This final day balances relaxation, unique luxury experiences, and a memorable send-off perfectly suited to a premium Vancouver itinerary.
